source_read: PMC HTML, PMC2561112 (Br J Clin Pharmacol 2008;66(4):430-443; title confirmed in own tab): all sections, Table 1 (as text), figure captions, acknowledgements, author information and article notes (received 16 Feb 2008, accepted 19 May 2008), reference list; no funding or competing-interest statement on the page. Figures 1-5: screenshot of own tab blank, figure image not viewable. With Ritter's editorial, PMC HTML PMC2561124 (Ritter JM, 'Prediction and Reverse Prediction in Therapeutics and Toxicology', BJCP 2008;66(4):427-429; labelled EDITORIAL; King's College London affiliation), read in full: two topics, of which only the section 'Beware drawing inferences from drug analyses in post-mortem samples' (2 paragraphs) concerns Ferner. Blind notes written before the card was opened. Table 1 correlations recomputed (Pearson, Spearman, Fisher z). Running-text paragraph counts per heading: The medical history 2; Qualitative post-mortem analysis 2; False-positive results 4; False-negative results 4; Quantitative post-mortem analysis 4 (Table 1 not counted); Importance of tolerance 2; Site-related and time-related differences 4; Transfer across barriers 4; Redistribution of absorbed drug 4; Influence of volume of distribution 6; Relationship between concentrations measured before and after death 4; Can the extent... 2; Making deduction... 3; Conclusion 1 (acknowledgement not counted).

key_findings.note: The 3rd paragraph is the one after Table 1.
All listed ratios match Table 1; range 1.4-4 confirmed.

Recomputed identically: Vd r 0.217 (p 0.24, n 31); raw P r 0.090; log P r 0.353 (p 0.048, n 32); C:P > Vd 9 of 31. Nuance: the 'not the sole determinant' sentence is attributed to other authors (reference 81); Ferner's own inference is the upper-limit point.
See missed: Rouzioux's imipramine 1.39 lies below the 2.58 minimum the review gives for the same series.
The source says 'heroin addicts'; the card's person-first rewording keeps the meaning.
All seven locators match my counts.

reporting_issues.note: Fisher z interval for 0.247 (n 31) is -0.12 to 0.55, recomputed. Spearman from Table 1: 0.32 for Vd (p 0.08) and 0.33 for log P (p 0.07).
Add: reference 75 (title: morphine in heroin overdose victims, human) is cited among animal studies for morphine (Relationship..., 2nd paragraph); reference 78 is the porcine study.

risk_of_bias.note: Editors' narrative-review checklist; overall some concerns, not milder than the worst domain.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. Small precision point in results_show: 'ratios from about 0.7' fits only the two carbon monoxide deaths (25-30% lower), or the chloroquine figure, which is ante-mortem:post-mortem (post-mortem:ante-mortem about 1.4). Every drug ratio the review lists is 1.0 (salicylate) or higher, so the human drug data run one way (higher after death). The Conclusion's 'no reliable or obvious connection' is broader than examples that include ratios near 1 (salicylate 1.0, paracetamol 1.5, moclobemide little redistribution).

missed: Internal inconsistency in the Rouzioux figures. Site-related and time-related differences, 1st paragraph: 8 of 10 cases had post-mortem left-ventricular concentrations 2.58 to 17.66 times those in life. Relationship..., 1st paragraph lists imipramine 1.39 for the same series, below that minimum; sample timing or site may differ but is not stated. The card repeats both (key finding 6; 1980 timeline entry) without noting the conflict.

The card calls Ritter the journal's Editor-in-Chief (design_detail, affiliations_note; 'the journal's editor' in where_it_stands). Neither PMC page states this: the piece is labelled EDITORIAL, written in the journal's 'we publish' voice, with a King's College London affiliation. Source the title or say 'the journal's editorial'.
